The Ministry of Ceremonies was one of the nine ministries of the Chinese Han dynasty. The Grand Master of Ceremonies was the chief official in charge of religious rites, rituals, prayers, and the maintenance of ancestral temples and altars. The role's title was changed to Upholder of Ceremonies from 195 to 144 BC before reverting to the original title. Although his main concern was to link the emperor with the supernatural world and Heaven, he was also given the task of setting educational standards for the Imperial University (est. 124 BC) and the academic chairs who specialized in the Five Classics, the canon of Confucianism.

Firstly this Unique National Wonders has an additional Civil Servant Slot, which allows for more Great Diplomats earlier than other Civilizations. Then it also gives more Spy Points, which even more directly enhances your Espionage potential. The other bonuses are to development, encouraging you to keep "We Love the Empress Day" in this City active as long as possible, subsidising the construction of Temples, and finally allowing Great Works to boost Food. This last effect you can first make use of in your Capital, and later in your new Cities as you move Great Works there to double-down on your other Unique Building's bonuses. Although you might not have room to concentrate on creating Great Works early on, your Spies might be able to help you explore alternative avenues to acquisition...
